front.title: MAP Tasks: Negotiation, Streaming Inference, Tools, Checkpoints, and Delegation

abstract.t: Defines the task layer of MAP: offer/quote/assign negotiation (with an optional bidding extension), streaming inference with credit-based flow control, tool invocation gated by requester-issued capability tokens, Merkle-committed transcripts with countersigned checkpoints, failure recovery by transcript replay, task delegation with budget and zone propagation, distributed memory/context retrieval, cancellation, and the task state machines for both roles.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Model
section.t: A task is a unit of remote work bound to one (requester, provider) pair, one capability, and one TaskID. Orchestration — decomposing a goal into a DAG of tasks, merging results — is application logic; MAP sees only tasks and (optionally) their parent/child delegation links. This keeps the protocol small and leaves merge strategy, scoring, and scheduling as local policy (critique C5), while giving orchestrators everything they need: verifiable per-task evidence, deterministic error semantics, and resumability.
TaskID = 32 random bytes chosen by the requester; it is the idempotency key: a provider receiving ASSIGN for a known TaskID MUST NOT start a second execution and SHOULD respond with current state.

Data ownership (normative): the requester is the source of truth for task terms (constraints, grants, budget); the provider is the source of truth for execution state; the countersigned transcript commitment (§8) is the only shared durable fact, and every cross-party claim — completion, usage, dispute — MUST be expressible against it. Neither party's local view is authoritative for the other; there is no distributed transaction between them, only signed messages, idempotent retries, and compensations (cancel-and-pay-to-boundary, §11). Ordering guarantees are scoped, never global: seq per session direction, chunk-seq per task.

section.name: Negotiation
section.sourcecode: Requester Provider | -- OFFER {task summary} ----------→ | (may be skipped: direct ASSIGN | ←-------------- QUOTE {terms} ----- | under a standing agreement) | -- ASSIGN {full task, terms ref} -→ | | ←------------------- ACCEPT ------- | (or REJECT{code})

Offer = { 1 => TaskID, 2 => CapURI, 3 => TaskConstraints, ? 4 => PayRef, ; pricing expectation (pay §3.1) ? 5 => Timestamp, ; offer expiry ? 6 => ExtMap ; negotiated extensions (e.g. ext-bid, §2.2) } TaskConstraints = { ? 1 => uint, ; max-context-tokens (hard) ? 2 => uint, ; max-output-tokens ? 3 => uint, ; deadline: wall-clock ms budget (hard) ? 4 => uint, ; ttft-ms guarantee requested (hard) ? 5 => ZoneLabel, ; task zone label (hard; §9) ? 6 => uint, ; min sandbox class (hard) ? 7 => Multihash, ; required model weights digest (hard if set) ? 8 => ExtMap } Quote = { 1 => TaskID, ? 2 => PayQuoteRef /*pay §3.1; absent = gratis or settlement out of band — payment is optional at the protocol layer*/, 3 => uint /*guaranteed ttft-ms*/, 4 => Timestamp /*expiry*/, ? 5 => ExtMap } Accept = { } ; empty content map Reject = { 1 => uint /*reason-code, §14*/ }
section.t: (Accept/Reject content maps assigned 2026-07-06 from TASK-007 FR-1; the negotiation diagram above showed them only inline.)

Fields marked hard MUST be satisfiable or the provider MUST REJECT (3xxx/4xxx); accepting then violating them is receipt-recordable breach. The quoted ttft-ms adopts design3's guarantee discipline: if the first CHUNK does not arrive within guarantee × 1.1, the requester SHOULD CANCEL (5001, retryable at other peers), fail over, and record the miss.

section.name: ASSIGN and payload transport
Bidding extension (OPTIONAL, extension key 1 = `ext-bid`)
section.t: Where markets are wanted, OFFER MAY be broadcast to k candidates; QUOTEs compete; the requester's selection function is local policy. ext-bid (extension key 1, core §5.1) is negotiated in HELLO (core §6.1 key 3) before use; peers that did not negotiate it MUST ignore its ExtMap entry.
The extension adds a single ExtMap entry (Offer key 6 / Quote key 5) keyed by the extension code point:
section.sourcecode: BidExt = { ; ExtMap value under ext key 1 1 => Timestamp, ; bid-deadline (QUOTEs after are late) ? 2 => uint ; queue-wait-ms (advertised backlog) }
section.t: bid-deadline (in an OFFER) bounds how long the requester collects QUOTEs; a provider's QUOTE received after it MAY be dropped. queue-wait-ms (in a QUOTE) is the provider's advertised current backlog, an input to the requester's local selection function only.
No auction clearing rules are standardized: selection stays local policy (they were dimensionally incoherent in the source designs — critique C5), so this extension defines fields, never a mechanism.

Security Considerations. queue-wait-ms is self-reported and therefore untrusted (critique C1): a provider can under-report backlog to win bids ("bid-sniping"). The requester's only defense is the trust projection — persistent under-delivery against advertised wait surfaces as poorer outcomes in dual-signed ExecutionReceipts (trust §8), so the lie is checkable ex post and repricing is local policy. bid-deadline is not a commitment device; it does not bind the provider.

section.name: Streaming: CHUNK
section.sourcecode: Chunk = { 1 => TaskID, 2 => uint, ; chunk-seq, from 0, dense 3 => uint, ; kind: 0 output-text, 1 output-bytes, ; 2 log, 3 usage-update, 4 tool-io 4 => bstr, ; content ? 5 => bool ; fin — last chunk of this kind }
section.t: Chunks flow under FLOW_CREDIT (core §8.1). A usage-update (kind 3) chunk's content is the deterministic CBOR encoding (core §4.2) of a Usage map — the §4 Complete key 4 shape {1 tokens-in, 2 tokens-out, 3 ttft-ms, 4 wall-ms} — with counters CUMULATIVE since task start; these are the meter readings pay §4.1 verifies watermarked invoices against, so a metered provider MUST emit one at or before each watermark it bills. Ordering is per chunk-seq; the transcript (§8.1) is defined over output-kind chunks in seq order, making audits unambiguous.

section.name: COMPLETE and output commitment
section.t: The requester verifies the transcript root against received chunks; match ⇒ it SHOULD issue/countersign the RECEIPT (trust §3) and settle (pay §5). Mismatch ⇒ 5000 + dispute path (pay §6). The signed COMPLETE is the provider's non-repudiable claim of what it produced (TH6, TH9).

section.name: Ranking guidance (informative)
section.t: Requesters typically shortlist via stable-plane constraints, refresh with STATUS, then rank by a local utility over: own-measured RTT/TTFT history, evidence-based trust per capability (trust §7), quoted price, and current queue. Weights are yours; publishing them invites gaming. Hard constraints are protocol; utility is not.

section.name: Reservations (capability `map:cap:schedule/reservation`)
section.t: Optional lease primitive for scarce resources: a requester sends RESERVE for a capability during a time window; the provider answers with a LEASE (granted / rejected / revoked). A granted lease is referenced by an ASSIGN's PayAgreeRef-adjacent flow (the lease id) and obliges the provider as below. Providers MAY require reservations by advertising accepting = 2 in STATUS. Leases are soft state with expiry; no distributed scheduler is defined (Kubernetes-style global scheduling is a non-goal — the mesh converges via prices and queues).
Message types: RESERVE 0x020F, LEASE 0x0210, LEASE_RELEASE 0x0211 (core §5).
section.sourcecode: Reserve = { ; msg-type 0x020F 1 => bstr .size 16, ; rsv-id (requester-chosen, unique) 2 => CapURI, ; reserved capability 3 => Timestamp, ; window start (from) 4 => Timestamp, ; window end (until) ? 5 => TaskConstraints, ; the work the lease will admit ? 6 => PayRef, ; holding-cost expectation (pay §3.1) ? 7 => ExtMap } Lease = { ; msg-type 0x0210 1 => bstr .size 16, ; rsv-id (echoes the Reserve) 2 => uint, ; status: 0 granted, 1 rejected, 2 revoked ? 3 => [Timestamp, Timestamp], ; granted window [from, until] ? 4 => PayQuoteRef, ; price of the hold (pay §3.1) ? 5 => ExtMap } LeaseRelease = { ; msg-type 0x0211 1 => bstr .size 16, ; rsv-id ? 2 => uint ; reason code (informational) }
section.t: State machine (per rsv-id): Requested (RESERVE sent) → Granted (LEASE status 0) → Active (during [from, until]) → Released (LEASE_RELEASE) / Expired (past until) / Revoked (LEASE status 2). A RESERVE MAY instead be answered with LEASE status 1 (Rejected), a terminal state.
Normative rules:

ul.li: The rsv-id is the idempotency key: a repeated RESERVE with the same

section.t: rsv-id and an identical window MUST be treated as a retransmission (the same LEASE re-sent), and a RESERVE reusing an rsv-id with a different window MUST be rejected (LEASE status 1) — silently re-scoping a live lease is forbidden.

ul.li: A granted LEASE's window (key 3, when present) MUST fall within the

section.t: RESERVE's requested [from, until]; a grant outside it is invalid and the requester MUST treat it as a rejection.

ul.li: While a lease is Active, the provider MUST ACCEPT a conforming ASSIGN

section.t: that references it (a task within the reserved capability and window and the RESERVE's constraints). A provider that fails to admit conforming work inside the window has missed the lease; the miss is receipt-recordable as a Failed outcome (outcome 1, trust §3) so the broken commitment is scored.

ul.li: A LEASE for an rsv-id whose requested window already lies entirely in

section.t: the past MUST be status 1 (rejected).

ul.li: LEASE_RELEASE is idempotent by rsv-id and voluntary; a released or

section.t: expired lease confers no obligation.
Overlapping reservations for the same resource are provider policy, not protocol — a provider MAY reject (status 1) or admit them at its own risk.

Security Considerations. The abuse is reservation squatting: cheaply holding scarce capacity to deny it to others. The mitigation is economic, not protocol-structural — RESERVE carries a PayRef (key 6) so the provider MAY price the hold (a non-refundable or escrowed holding cost via the pay layer, pay §3), making squatting cost money. A provider under sustained lease-DoS SHOULD fall back to shorter windows and higher holding costs; both are local policy. Because a missed lease is receipt-recordable, a provider that grants leases it cannot honor accrues negative trust (trust §8), which bounds over-committing.

section.name: Tool invocation
section.t: Direction inversion is the crux: during execution the provider asks the requester for permission to run a tool. Authorization is a capability token — a DelegationCert (identity §4) issued by the requester, pinned to this TaskID, naming allowed tool URIs and caveats:
section.sourcecode: Provider Requester | -- TOOL_CALL {task, tool-uri, --→ | policy check (allowlist, zone, | args-digest} | sandbox class, budget) | ←- TOOL_GRANT {DelegationCert --- | caveats: task-id, tool-uri, | w/ caveats} -------- | args-digest, expiry (<=60s), | -- TOOL_RESULT {output, digest} -→ | max-invocations
section.t: Rules: providers MUST NOT execute tools absent a valid unexpired grant whose caveats cover the exact call (args-digest binds the arguments); grants are single-task, non-redelegable by default; Zone-2 execution additionally requires SecurityProfile sandbox ≥ container and the tool on the provider's advertised allowlist (TH7, TH15). Tool I/O appears in the transcript as kind-4 chunks — auditable end to end.

section.name: Transcript commitment
section.t: transcript-root = the Merkle root (suite hash H) over the output/tool chunks (kinds 0, 1, 4) in chunk-seq order, constructed as follows:
section.sourcecode: leaf(c) = H(0x00 || enc([c.chunk-seq, c.kind, c.content])) ; enc = deterministic CBOR (core §4.2) of the triple — ; bare concatenation would be ambiguous across ; variable-length fields parent(l, r) = H(0x01 || l || r) ; domain-separated from leaves odd node = promoted unchanged to the next level empty root = H(0x00 || enc([])) ; zero output chunks
section.t: Incremental, streaming-friendly, and shared by checkpoints, COMPLETE, receipts, and disputes — one commitment structure everywhere. The 0x00/ 0x01 domain separation prevents leaf/interior confusion attacks; the CBOR leaf encoding makes leaves injective in (seq, kind, content).

section.name: CHECKPOINT / CHECKPOINT_ACK
section.t: Providers SHOULD checkpoint every N output tokens (default 512) or at tool boundaries. The requester replies CHECKPOINT_ACK containing its own signature over (TaskID, chunk-seq, root) — the countersignature that makes a checkpoint a valid resumption point (critique C11: never resume from state attested only by the party that just failed or may be malicious).

section.name: Resumption
section.t: On provider loss, the requester selects a successor and sends RESUME: {TaskID, last countersigned checkpoint, the output transcript so far (inline or content-addressed), original ASSIGN terms}. The successor re-warms by transcript replay — reprocessing prompt + prior output as context — and continues from chunk-seq+1. Determinism across heterogeneous engines is not assumed; the seam at the resumption point is permitted and visible in the transcript (marked by a kind-2 log chunk).

section.name: Opaque state / KV-cache (extension key 2 = `ext-kvx`)
section.t: Engine-state blobs (Checkpoint.4) MAY shortcut re-warm only between peers running the identical engine+model+quantization, and only within Zone ≤1 or with TEE attestation — normative resumption remains replay (critique C10). ext-kvx (extension key 2, core §5.1) is HELLO-negotiated (core §6.1 key 3) and never required for conformance.
Payload container (the only structure this revision fixes):
section.sourcecode: KvxExt = { ; ExtMap value under ext key 2 1 => uint, ; container version 2 => bstr ; opaque engine-state blob }
section.t: A receiver MUST reject a KvxExt outside Zone ≤1 unless the sender is TEE-attested (zone enforcement, §9). Engine-fingerprint matching (which engine+model+quantization tuples are interchangeable) and the blob's internal format are deferred: this section reserves the code point and the container; full semantics are future work. An implementation that does not understand a received KvxExt MUST fall back to replay resumption.

section.name: Zone enforcement (normative)
section.t: The task zone label (Constraints.5) governs everything attached to the task: ASSIGN MUST NOT go to a peer whose zone level exceeds the label (arch Z1); InputSpec content-addressed fetches of proprietary blocks are Zone ≤1; TOOL_GRANTs inherit the label; DELEGATE (§10) propagates it and MAY only tighten it (Z2). Violations: 2004, non-retryable, receiptable. The Git-workspace extension (ext-git, extension key 3, core §5.1, from design3) — shallow, path-scoped, token-gated clone/push over a dedicated stream — is defined for Zone ≤1 only and MUST be rejected in Zone ≥2. ext-git is HELLO-negotiated (core §6.1 key 3). Payload container:
section.sourcecode: GitExt = { ; ExtMap value under ext key 3 1 => uint, ; container version 2 => bstr ; opaque git-workspace parameters }
section.t: A receiver MUST reject a GitExt in Zone ≥2 (2004, non-retryable, receiptable). The clone/push protocol details (shallow depth, path scoping, token gating, stream framing) are deferred: this reserves the code point, the container, and the zone restriction; full semantics are future work. Peers that did not negotiate ext-git MUST ignore its ExtMap entry.

section.name: Delegation of tasks
section.t: A provider MAY subcontract via DELEGATE-linked child tasks when the ASSIGN carries caveat delegable ≥ 1. The child ASSIGN embeds the parent chain (delegation depth decrements; budget caveats split; zone tightens-only). The root requester's receipt evidence names the whole chain, so accountability survives subcontracting. Default is non-delegable.

section.name: Cancellation
section.t: CANCEL content { 1 => TaskID, 2 => uint /reason-code, §14/ } (field numbers assigned 2026-07-06 from TASK-007 FR-1) from either side; provider stops within one chunk boundary, emits a final CHECKPOINT and COMPLETE(outcome=partial). Usage to the countersigned boundary is payable (pay §4); this makes cancellation cheap to honor and removes the incentive to ignore it.

section.name: Memory / context retrieval
section.t: Peers advertising MemoryTopics (discovery §2) serve:

The embedding-model id MUST match an advertised MemoryTopic (similarity across embedding spaces is undefined — critique). Thresholds are query parameters, not protocol constants. Retrieved context enters InputSpec as ContextRefs with provenance, so poisoned context is attributable (TH6/TH7).

section.name: Task state machines
section.t: Requester view:
section.sourcecode: CREATED -OFFER→ QUOTED -ASSIGN→ PENDING -ACCEPT→ ACTIVE | | |‐REJECT→ FAILED(f) ACTIVE -CHUNK*→ ACTIVE | └-expiry→ FAILED(f) ACTIVE -CHECKPOINT/ACK→ ACTIVE └(direct ASSIGN)→ PENDING ACTIVE -provider loss→ SUSPENDED SUSPENDED -RESUME(new peer)→ ACTIVE ACTIVE -COMPLETE(ok)→ DELIVERED ACTIVE|SUSPENDED -CANCEL→ CANCELLED DELIVERED -verify root→ SETTLING -pay/receipt→ CLOSED any -unrecoverable 2xxx/5xxx→ FAILED DELIVERED -root mismatch→ DISPUTED (pay §6)
section.t: Provider view: IDLE → QUOTING → COMMITTED (on ACCEPT; resources reserved) → EXECUTING ⇄ CHECKPOINTING → DELIVERED → SETTLED, with CANCELLED and FAILED exits mirroring the above. Providers MUST bound COMMITTED-without- ASSIGN-traffic by the quote expiry.

section.name: Error handling and retries
section.t: Retryable-at-same-peer: 4000/4001 (backoff per retry-after-ms), 1005. Retry-elsewhere: 5001 TTFT miss, 4002, 3001. Non-retryable without change: 2xxx, 3002, 5004, 5005. Idempotent re-ASSIGN with the same TaskID is always safe (§1). Orchestrator fallback chains (local → trusted mesh → gateway) are thereby deterministic — the property design3 wanted from "aggressive fallbacks", now grounded in error semantics.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Tool gating (§7) and zone rules (§9) are the primary injection/exfiltration controls; transcripts+countersigned checkpoints give attributable execution and safe resumption; flow credit bounds provider exposure; TaskID idempotency prevents replayed ASSIGN double-execution (with core §7). Providers remain exposed to semantically malicious inputs — sandboxing requirements are the floor, not a guarantee; meshes SHOULD gate Zone-2 tool execution behind stricter sandbox classes than the default.

section.name: IANA-Style Considerations
section.t: Registers: chunk kinds; reservation/lease fields; caveat keys delegable, budget, args-digest; extensions ext-bid (key 1, complete, §2.2), ext-kvx (key 2, stub, §8.4), ext-git (key 3, stub, §9) — assigned in core §5.1. The assigned values and the family-wide index are in draft-map-wire-01.md §3.13, §3.14, and §3.15 (extension keys in §3.4); in case of divergence the normative definitions in §3, §6, §7, §8, and §9 govern.
